name: Grevel's House

dates.built: possibly C14, remodelled C17 and C19
dates.note: THE ENTRY REFUSES THE ATTRIBUTION THE BUILDING'S NAME CARRIES. It says the house is 'not necessarily the home of William Grevil; the "flower of the wool merchants of all England" who died circa 1400', and that it was 'Thought to have been a mediaeval barn, possibly C14, converted to dwelling'. A Chipping Campden town website read the same day says flatly 'Built in 1380 by William Grevel'. The refusal is Historic England's and the attribution is the town's; neither is resolved here and the exemplar's `why` is written from the entry rather than from the name.

quotes.text: 2. Externally partly mediaeval with Cl7 and C19 remodellings. Thought to have been a mediaeval barn, possibly C14, converted to dwelling and converted in late C16 when the 'Grevil bay' was imported. A complex and enigmatic building - not necessarily the home of William Grevil; the 'flower of the wool merchants of all England' who died circa 1400.

note: Tranche 3, the English cottage and the Cotswold vernacular, 5 Sep 2026. Added by this tranche. The building is here because the node's central claim -- that a Perpendicular Gothic window detail survives in working use for centuries -- has to rest on a building where the detail is at full strength, and this is that building: a two-storey traceried bay of six lights, with king mullions in the gable beside it. The entry is unusually candid that the house is 'complex and enigmatic' and refuses the attribution the name asserts.
